refuter_findings.location: ## Open problem, the perturbative comparison, OPE truncation, and stress-energy clauses; title “Four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence and mass gap”
refuter_findings.evidence: [Jaffe–Witten §4](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/yangmills.pdf), printed p. 141 / standalone PDF p. 6, says: “Correlation functions of the quantum field operators should agree at short distances with the predictions of asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization theory.” It also describes a stress tensor and an OPE with prescribed singularities, but does not state the item’s all-order little-o remainders, dimension-truncation scaling-degree bound, or cutoff-independent spacetime-smearing limit, nor establish their equivalence to its formulation. The item’s Status calls these requirements for a solution, while the statement and page present the unqualified Clay problem; this is a strengthened formulation without established equivalence.

refuter_findings.location: ## Open problem, paragraph beginning “For the required gauge-field content” (canonical dimensions clause)
refuter_findings.evidence: The statement says the polynomials are field labels and defines “[P]” as the maximum monomial dimension of a polynomial label. The zero polynomial is included by that definition but has no monomials, so this maximum is undefined. Later clauses use [P_i] and [P] in rescaling and OPE exponents, without excluding the zero label or assigning it a convention.

reader_findings.location: ## Open problem: paragraphs beginning “The perturbative comparison data are fixed as follows” and “The theory also has a local symmetric stress-energy tensor”; title “Four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence and mass gap”.
reader_findings.evidence: Jaffe–Witten §4 (MPPc printed pp. 141–142; standalone PDF §4, p. 6) states broad short-distance agreement with asymptotic freedom and perturbative renormalization, including a stress tensor and an OPE with prescribed local singularities. The item adds specific all-order little-o remainders for correlations and Wilson coefficients, a dimension-truncation scaling-degree bound, and a cutoff-independent spacetime-smearing limit for the stress tensor. The cited formulation does not state these quantitative conditions or establish their equivalence to its broad requirements. Unless supported as equivalent, they define a strengthened problem while the title presents the Clay problem without qualification.
